extracted.intended_audience: prospective auctioneers and gastronomic agents; general Victorian readers interested in social/professional advice
extracted.subtask_description: Satirical practical guidance for two professions (auctioneer; 'gastronomic agent' / dinner-master), specifying personal qualities, professional conduct, services to offer, and how to present/market oneself to clients and tradesmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pomposity; use honest titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ape higher rank or use inflated titles (e.g., a bagman should not call himself the 'representative' of Dobson and Hobson; an auctioneer should not call his room his 'study').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pomposity is vulgar—use common, honest designations (private room, office). The auctioneer 'will not call himself an “advocate,” but an auctioneer.' Avoid big titles intended to awe people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty in representation of goods and clients
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer/dinner-master 'must not sacrifice his honesty ... nor tell fibs about himself or them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While expected to take a favorable, kindly view and praise what 'can fairly be said,' he should not 'draw the long bow' for clients; praise should be truthful and ingeniously framed rather than fictitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental qualities: truth, imagination, wit, benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: An auctioneer 'should have the organ of truth large; of imagination and comparison, considerable; of wit, great; of benevolence, excessively large.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These faculties equip him to praise honestly, to compare and contextualize items, to entertain, and to be kindly toward sellers and buyers—central professional virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural literacy in lighter literature and tasteful criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer 'should be elegantly conversant' with lighter literature, able to give a neat history of the author, sparkling criticism of the work, and an appropriate eulogium upon the binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to avoid heavy antiquarian/philological works; be competent in fashionable tastes so as to attract and educate buyers (or at least to entice purchases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine enthusiasm and ability to assume characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer 'must feel these things' and 'be every one of the characters to whom he addresses himself'—a 'glass in which all the tastes of fashion are reflected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affectation is no substitute for real feeling; authenticity of enthusiasm makes the persuasion effective and agreeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and gentlemanliness / social polish
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer should have 'had an education in the midst of the best company' and 'an insight into the most delicate feelings, and wants, and usages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social refinement and knowledge of high society are necessary to appeal to fashionable clientele and to perform the role gracefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eloquent oratory and entertainment value
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer's 'pulpit oratory' is invaluable; he should be able to 'cause streams of world-philosophy to flow' from trivial objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public speaking skill and the ability to draw moral/witty points from items will attract audiences and elevate sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as impartial protector of the host (not a provisioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dinner-master should not be merely a provider of meat or wine but a gentleman who 'sees that the [client] is not cheated by his tradesmen.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent's value is in impartial supervision and quality control, not in selling produce for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and peculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent 'must not be a ruined gastronomist' who would be tempted to make bargains with tradesmen or accept presents; such peculation would ruin the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select subordinates and suppliers carefully; maintain financial integrity and independence from tradesmen to preserve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gendered suitability (author's assertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author asserts that women 'cannot give a great dinner' and are 'bad dinner-caterers'—a prescriptive claim on who should perform the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit (period) opinion used to argue the role requires a man's understanding and dedication; it reflects the author's social bias and is presented as a justification for a male agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social rank and titular branding
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent 'must be as high-born as possible' and ideally able to tack an honorific to his name (e.g., 'THE HONORABLE GEORGE GORMAND GOBBLETON') on cards and signage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An air of nobility and a distinguished professional card (gilt arms, baronet's hand, Gothic letters) will attract clients who defer to rank—branding and perceived pedigree are part of the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornamented staging: French affectation and office decor
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent should use French in language, employ a French valet, have richly furnished chambers with cookery books, sample bottles, truffles, busts of famed chefs, and framed historic menus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A carefully curated environment and cosmopolitan affectation (French words, truffles, busts of Ude/Careme) create credibility with vulgar clients who equate French tastes with refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal appearance and props
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent should present as a 'portly grave man' with an 'enormous gold chain,' 'one large diamond ring,' and a gold snuff-box to thrust into a visitor's hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consistent personal brand—dress, accessories, manner—helps persuade clients of the agent's authority and genteel taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide trustworthy cooks (list of vetted cooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gastronomic Agent 'engages to provide ... cooks to dress the dinners; a list of which gentlemen he has by him, and will recommend none who are not worthy of the strictest confidence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a roster of reliable, vouched-for cooks; vet character and competence before recommending them to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a menu appropriate to the price
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent will supply 'a menu for the table, according to the price which the Amphitryon chooses to incur.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design menus tailored to budget and occasion; do not promise dishes outside the agreed price-tier without consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source suppliers and correspond internationally when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent will 'provide them with viands, fruit, wine, &c., sending to Paris, if need be, where he has a regular correspondence with Messrs. Chevet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain supplier networks domestically and abroad; the ability to procure special items (via Paris, etc.) is part of the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply dexterous waiters and control household servants
rubrics_metrics.description: He has 'a list of dexterous table-waiters ... and would strongly recommend that the servants of the house should be locked in the back-kitchen or servants' hall during the time the dinner takes place.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide trained front-of-house staff and limit interference from the host's usual servants to ensure service quality and avoid mishaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and audit tradesmen accounts; refuse gratuities
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'will receive and examine all the accounts of the fournisseurs ... pledging his honor ... not to receive one shilling of paltry gratification from the tradesmen ... but to see that the bills are more moderate, and their goods of better quality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as an auditor for suppliers' bills, negotiate and certify reasonable charges, and publicly commit to refusing bribes to maintain client trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee and client trust: five guineas; clients must trust the Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: His fee 'for superintending a dinner will be five guineas' and he 'entreats his clients to trust ENTIRELY to him and his subordinates ... NOT TO THINK of inserting dishes of their own invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear pricing and require client deference to the Agent's plan to preserve the ensemble of the dinner; any client-requested deviations must be mediated through the Agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation hours and importance of personal interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent 'will be at home for consultation from ten o'clock until two ... a PERSONAL INTERVIEW is always the best' to assess 'number but the character of the guests ... whether they are fond of any particular wine or dish, what is their state of health, rank, style, profession, &c.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize face-to-face consultations to gather guest profiles, dietary restrictions, and social context; tailor menus and service accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field rounds schedule and service availability
rubrics_metrics.description: He lays out a detailed rounds schedule (2–3 Russell Square, 3–3¾ Harley Street, etc.) and notes he 'will NOT go to the palace, where it is utterly impossible to serve a good dinner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a predictable itinerary for client visits and set boundaries on locations/times where quality service is impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize weekly trial-dinners to vet tradesmen and samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Monday evening 'the Gastronomic Agent proposes to give a series of trial-dinners' where tradesmen supply food gratis and wine-merchants compete by sending samples and tickets of prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use curated trial events to evaluate suppliers, collect price information, and publicly reward those who meet standards; keep records (receipts) for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a very keen judge of food and wine
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent is 'a VERY KEEN JUDGE,' capable of recognizing age/primeness of meat and freshness of fish at a glance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and demonstrate acute sensory judgment in food and vintages; this technical competence underpins professional credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small professional falsehoods are permissible (marketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text suggests 'there can't be much harm in an innocent fib of that sort; for the gastronomic agent must be a sort of dinner-pope, whose opinions cannot be supposed to err.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author tolerates modest exaggeration of credentials as a marketing device to gain client confidence—presented as a pragmatic (if ethically questionable) tactic.
